11.16 Effect of Pressure on Melting Point of Substance Do you Know? i. An avalanche originates when a large amount of snow collects at a location. ii. A large iceberg melts at the base but not at the top.

Same physics is behind these two phenomena. In both activities, main role is of pressure. Melting point of solid is greatly affected by pressure applied on it. The effect of pressure on melting point is different for different substances. For the substances like cast iron and ice whose volume decreases while melting, their

melting point decreases with increase in pressure. For the substances like wax and lead whose volume increases while melting, their melting point increases with increase in pressure. When two pieces of ice are pressed against each other, pressure on the contact portion increases and hence melting point decreases to that portion. As a result, ice melts in contact portion. If applied pressure is removed again, the melting point increases to initial value. Now water, so formed after melting of ice, freezes. During this process two pieces of ice join to form a single piece. Hence, when pressure is applied to ice, it melts and as soon as the pressure is removed, it freezes again. We refer to this phenomenon as regelation. Regelation is the phenomenon of melting of ice under the application of pressure/compression and its freezing after the removal of applied pressure. Why is it difficult to walk on the surface of a frozen lake? 11.17 Phase Diagram and Triple Point [Fig. 11.8, phase diagram for water A graph between pressure and temperature which has three curves; namely fusion curve, vaporization curve and sublimation curve is called phase diagram. It is also called P-T diagram.
Physics, Grade 11 | 265
The phase diagram clearly explains the three different phases of a matter. The phase diagram of water is shown in figure 11.8.

a. Vaporization curve (steam line): The graph showing variation of boiling point of a substance with the pressure is called vaporization curve. The substance exists in liquid state above the steam line and it exists in gaseous state below steam line.

b. Fusion curve (Ice line): The graph showing the variation of the melting point of substance with pressure is called fusion curve. A substance exists in solid state above the ice line and it exists in liquid state below ice line.

c. Sublimation curve (Hoar-frost line): The graph showing the variation of sublimation point of substance with pressure is called sublimation curve or hoar-frost line. At very low temperature and pressure, substances are found to sublimate. For example, solid carbon dioxide (dry ice) sublimates even at atmospheric pressure. A substance exists in solid state above the hoar-frost line and it exists in gaseous state below hoarfrost line.
Triple Point Triple point of a substance is the point in P-T diagram representing a particular value of temperature and pressure at which all three states of that substance can co-exist.

Triple point of a substance can also be defined as the point in phase diagram at which vaporization curve, fusion curve and sublimation curve of given substance intersect each other. The triple point of water is (0.006 atm., 0.01°C) and that of carbon dioxide is (5.11 atm., – 56.6°C)
